key_insight: Axion compiles an entire differentiable finite element simulation into a GPU-native JAX program, accelerating demanding phase-field fracture analyses.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables large-scale fracture simulation and parameter sensitivities for applications spanning hydraulic fracture, dental mechanics, and concrete dams.
method: JIT-compile element kernels, nonlinear solvers, damage constraints, and load increments for execution without host intervention.
Use forward-mode automatic differentiation for consistent tangents and differentiate the solver program for parameter sensitivities.
Combine matrix-free operators, fixed-array octree refinement, and cell-based multi-GPU domain decomposition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 37.9× speedup over single-CPU FEniCSx at identical 2D discretization, 92% strong and 96% weak scaling efficiency on four GPUs, and a 96M-DOF dam simulation on one GPU.
watch_item: The headline speedup compares one GPU with one CPU, so it should not be interpreted as a hardware-matched measure of algorithmic advantage.
paper_title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
